ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: <image>In $\odot P, P D=10, P Q=10,$ and $Q E=20$, find PE
ready1_open_rewrite.title: Geometry3K open-ended problem

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a circle with P as the center, and P is inside the circle. Below there is a chord passing through C, Q, and E, with E on the circle; segment PQ is drawn from P to this chord, and there is a right-angle mark at Q, indicating PQ ⟂ CE. The problem gives PQ = 10, QE = 20. Reasoning: Because PQ is perpendicular to chord CE, triangle PQE is a right triangle at Q. PE is the radius from the center P to a point E on the circle, and is also the hypotenuse of right triangle PQE. Therefore, by the Pythagorean theorem, PE = sqrt(PQ^2 + QE^2) = sqrt(10^2 + 20^2) = sqrt(100 + 400) = sqrt(500) = 10√5.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify P as the center of the circle and Q as the foot of a perpendicular from P to the lower chord CE, with E on the circle. Read from the text that PQ = 10 and QE = 20. Use the theorem that a perpendicular from the center to a chord bisects the chord and also note that triangle PQE is right at Q. Since PE is a radius and is the hypotenuse of right triangle PQE, compute PE = sqrt(PQ^2 + QE^2) = sqrt(10^2 + 20^2) = 10 sqrt(5).

method.method_draft: Set up coordinates based on the diagram. From the image, take P as the center of the circle and let Q be the point on the lower chord where the perpendicular from P meets the chord. Place P at (0,0) and choose the chord CE to be horizontal, so Q can be placed at (0,-10) or equivalently at distance 10 from P. Since QE = 20 along the chord, place E 20 units horizontally from Q, for example E = (20,-10). Then PE is the distance from the origin to E: PE = sqrt(20^2 + 10^2) = 10 sqrt(5).
method.CoT_raw: Image description: The diagram shows circle \(\odot P\) with center \(P\). A lower chord runs through points \(C\) and \(E\), and point \(Q\) lies on this chord. The segment \(PQ\) is drawn perpendicular to the chord at \(Q\), as indicated by the right-angle mark. Segment \(QE\) is along the chord from \(Q\) to \(E\). Reasoning: Set coordinates as in the assigned method. Put \(P=(0,0)\). Since \(PQ=10\), place \(Q=(0,-10)\). Rotate the coordinate system so the chord through \(Q\) and \(E\) is horizontal. Since \(QE=20\), place \(E=(20,-10)\). Then \(PE\) is the distance from the origin to \(E\): \(PE=\sqrt{20^2+10^2}=\sqrt{400+100}=\sqrt{500}=10\sqrt{5}\).
